description: We're a tech-driven team with experience in cybersecurity, AI, and detection engineering. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we're tackling the MODIS & VIIRS Hot Spots challenge to turn satellite data into meaningful wildfire insights. Our goal is to build an intelligent monitoring platform that detects unusual patterns and visualizes fire activity. We're looking for passionate teammates skilled in Data Science, GIS, Machine Learning, Web Development, and UI/UX.
summary: When a day looks quiet on a fire map, what did the satellites actually see? Insider Lens brings NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS fire detections into one calendar and keeps the source of each observation visible. In our southern Canada study area, VIIRS recorded detections on 27 days in June 2023. Adding MODIS brought the total to 28. On June 1, Terra MODIS recorded two detections that a VIIRS-only calendar leaves out. Fire analysts and land managers can use the map to trace a day back to its source before drawing conclusions about local fire history.
details:
On June 1, 2023, a fire analyst looking at our southern Canada study area would see a blank day with VIIRS selected. Switching on MODIS reveals two Terra detections, both recorded at 18:41 UTC. Insider Lens lets the analyst trace those observations back to their source and see why the calendar changed.

We built an interactive map and fire activity calendar using NASA FIRMS observations from Terra and Aqua MODIS and Suomi NPP VIIRS. We group records by 10 km equal-area grid cell and UTC date while preserving the original sensor and record count. Users can select a region and month, compare either sensor family or both, inspect a day on the map, and export the same selection as a CSV.

In the June 2023 study area, combining both sources preserved detections on 28 days, compared with 27 for VIIRS alone. Across 568 cell-days with detections, 34 appeared only in MODIS, 199 appeared in both, and 335 appeared only in VIIRS. This helps analysts and land managers check whether a gap reflects their choice of sensor. Different satellite overpass times and coverage limit what a blank day can tell us about fires on the ground.

We built the interface with React, TypeScript, Vite, and MapLibre GL JS. Python, SQLite, and pyproj handle the data. A separate verification program checked exact counts across 12 test cases, and Playwright tested the browser workflows.
